chunks: And with this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, that he ascribed it to Sa'd ibn Turaif, from Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Al-Harith al-A'war, that he said:
The Commander of the Believers, Allah's blessings be upon him, said to Hasan, his son, peace be upon him: O my son, what is manliness? He said: Chasteness and rectification of property.

key_terms.إِصْلَاحُ الْمَالِ: Rectification or proper management of wealth/property
key_terms.الْمُرُوءَةُ: Manliness, virtue, or nobility of character

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of manliness (Muru'ah) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (AS) elicits from Imam Hasan (AS) a concise definition of *al-muru'ah* (virtue/manliness) as comprising *al-'iffah* (chastity/modesty) and *islah al-mal* (proper management of wealth). This pairing highlights the Shia ethical ideal that true nobility requires both internal spiritual purity and external financial integrity, ensuring one remains independent and capable of fulfilling social and religious obligations.

en.basel-kadem: 4.	With this chain of narrators, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from some of our companions, that he ascribed it to Sa’d bin Turaif, from Asbagh bin Nubata, from Harith, the half-blinded, that he said:
The Commander of the Believers, Allah’s blessings be upon him, said to Hasan, his son, peace be upon him: O my son, what is manliness? He said: Chasteness and rectification of property.
